articles.title: Police seek help to locate Lebron Blake wanted on recall to prison
articles.excerpt: Police are appealing for assistance in locating Lebron Blake, who is wanted on recall to prison and has links to the Rochdale area.
articles.content_html:
Police are appealing for help to find a man from Oldham who is wanted on recall to prison. Lebron Blake, born on 6 October 2005, is known to have connections to the Oldham, Bury and Rochdale areas of Greater Manchester.

Authorities have urged anyone with information regarding Blake's whereabouts to contact them. They can be reached at 0161 856 8982 or through Crimestoppers.

The appeal follows concerns about Blake's compliance with the terms of his release. Police are keen to locate him as soon as possible to ensure public safety.

Anyone with information can find Greater Manchester Police and Crimestoppers contact details at the end of this article.

articles.title: Failed asylum seeker jailed for bringing weapons to Heywood school
articles.excerpt: A man has been sentenced to two years in prison after taking a hammer, hatchet and kitchen knife to a school in Heywood to attract attention to his asylum case.
articles.content_html:
A man has been sentenced to two years in prison after taking a hammer, a hatchet and a kitchen knife to a school in Heywood. Both Douk Deng, 21, a South Sudanese national, was jailed after he was found on the premises of Edgar Wood Academy on August 6 last year.

Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Deng had become increasingly frustrated with immigration authorities for not providing assistance in his bid to stay in the UK. He had applied for and been refused asylum on three occasions. Deng intended to 'create a scene for attention' to aid his cause, the court was told.

Deng was arrested after workmen confronted him at the school, which was closed to pupils for the summer. A member of the public had raised the alarm after observing him behaving oddly while carrying a petrol can with a hammer tied to his belt. He was seen mumbling as he walked around the school before builders called the police due to their concerns.

The court's decision reflects the seriousness of Deng's actions and the potential risk posed to the community. His behaviour was described as alarming, particularly in a school environment.

articles.title: Three Sentenced for Role in Rochdale's Adam Drugs Line
articles.excerpt: Two men and a teenager have been sentenced for their involvement in a Rochdale drugs line that generated over £1 million annually, despite previous police efforts to dismantle it.
articles.content_html:
Two drug dealers have been sentenced for their involvement in a notorious drugs line in Rochdale, which continued operating despite multiple police interventions. Haider Ali, 34, known as 'The Ghost', and Alan Ronald Ohara, 47, referred to as 'Rocket Ronny', were arrested last year while running the 'Adam Line', which was previously exposed in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG.

During a police operation, officers observed what appeared to be a drug deal on Baron Street. They followed a Nissan Qashqai, and upon stopping the vehicle, Ali attempted to flee but was apprehended nearby. He was found with £1,000 in cash and wraps of cocaine and heroin. Police also discovered 75 wraps of cocaine and 32 wraps of heroin on the dashboard of the car.

The third person arrested was 17-year-old Shane Walsh, who acted as Ali's 'trusted lieutenant'. Evidence indicated that Walsh had been involved in drug dealing since he was 16. His mobile phone contained lists of debts and expenses related to his role in the operation, and he continued to deal drugs even after being released on bail.

The court heard that Ohara was more than just a driver; he was involved in the management of the drugs line and had discussed starting his own operation. Defence counsel for Walsh stated that he had been a victim of grooming and exploitation, having moved to Rochdale from Middleton due to issues at home.

articles.title: Rochdale Police Launch Knife Amnesty Scheme
articles.excerpt: Rochdale police have introduced a knife amnesty scheme, allowing residents to anonymously dispose of knives and bladed weapons at designated bins across the district.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale police have launched a "Forever Amnesty" scheme, enabling residents to safely and anonymously dispose of knives and bladed weapons. The initiative features 13 permanent amnesty bins located across ten local districts, with three bins specifically situated in the Rochdale district.

The scheme aims to reduce knife crime and promote community safety by providing a secure method for individuals to surrender dangerous items without fear of prosecution.

Residents can find the amnesty bins at various locations throughout Rochdale, encouraging participation from the community to help create a safer environment.

This initiative is part of a broader effort by local authorities to address concerns surrounding knife crime and to foster a culture of safety within the community.

articles.title: Investigation Launched After Fire at Illegal Waste Site in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: The Environment Agency has confirmed an investigation into a fire at an illegal waste site in Smallbridge, which required extensive firefighting efforts over the weekend.
articles.content_html:
An investigation has been launched following a fire at a waste site in Smallbridge. Crews worked throughout the night on Friday, July 24, after a fire broke out off Spring Mill Walk. Thick plumes of smoke were visible for miles around, prompting a significant response from emergency services.

Firefighters were called to the scene at 8.15pm and worked until around 1pm the following day to extinguish the fire. Six fire engines and specialist equipment were deployed to tackle the blaze, which involved a large quantity of waste at the site.

The Environment Agency became involved due to the nature of the incident and confirmed that the fire occurred at an illegal waste site. An update issued on August 1 stated that the site is now under investigation following the incident.

Residents in the surrounding area were advised to keep their windows and doors closed during the firefighting efforts to avoid smoke inhalation. The investigation will determine the circumstances surrounding the fire and the status of the site.

articles.title: Man arrested on suspicion of attempted rape in Rochdale parks
articles.excerpt: A man in his 20s has been arrested on suspicion of attempted rape following two sex attacks in Rochdale parks on Saturday morning.
articles.content_html:
A man in his 20s has been arrested on suspicion of attempted rape following two sex attacks in Rochdale on Saturday morning, July 25. The incidents, which are being treated as linked, occurred less than two hours apart in Broadfield Park and Milnrow Memorial Park.

The first incident was reported to police at around 6:15am, where a woman reported being sexually assaulted by a stranger. The second incident occurred at 8:38am, with another woman also stating she had been attacked by a man she did not know. Both women provided similar descriptions of the attacker, prompting police to issue a description of a black male believed to be wearing a three-piece suit or smart black clothes and a dark coat, and carrying a briefcase.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) confirmed that a robust investigation is underway, with CCTV enquiries showing a suspect leaving the Coco Lounge in Rochdale town centre at 5am. In an update issued later, GMP stated that the man remains in custody for questioning as enquiries continue. Specialist officers are supporting the victims during this time.

Police are continuing to gather information related to the incidents. Anyone with information is urged to contact GMP on 101, quoting incident numbers 79 and 880 of 25/07/2026, or to use the LiveChat service on the force website. Information can also be passed anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.
